:::{#rem-angle-well-defined}
#### Why the angle is well defined

The [cosine similarity](#def-cosine-similarity) is defined, because both vectors are nonzero (@thm-norm-properties).
By @thm-cauchy-schwarz, it lies in the [closed interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-closed-interval) $[-1, 1]$,
which is where the [arccosine](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-arccosine), $\arccos$, is defined.
So the angle $\angpar$ lies in $[0, \pi]$, with [cosine](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-cosine-sine) $\cos\angpar = \cossim(\vecf{x}, \vecf{y})$.

:::
